title: The Iron in Your Blood Came From a Dying Star
_accuracy: Science: iron forms via stellar nucleosynthesis and is dispersed by supernovae — its origin is genuinely cosmic. Framed as a reflection/sign, not as 'proof'. Ayah 57:25 ('wa anzalnā al-ḥadīd' — 'and We sent down iron') is pulled live from Quran.com; narrator reads the meaning (copyright-clean, no reciter). Every beat gets its own matched cosmic clip.

beats.say: Every bit of iron on Earth was forged inside a dying star. And delivered here, from space.
Not made in a lab. Not dug out of nothing. Forged at temperatures of billions of degrees.
Iron can't be made on a planet. It's born in the heart of massive stars. Then flung out when they die.
So the iron in your blood, in your bones, is the ash of dead stars.
You are, quite literally, made of stardust.
Now here's what stops people. Fourteen hundred years ago, the Quran didn't say iron was made here. It said it was sent down.
And We sent down iron, in which is great strength, and benefits for the people.
The very element running through your veins was born in an explosion halfway across the galaxy.
And a book, in the desert, called it a gift sent down. Fourteen centuries early. Follow for the signs people scroll straight past.

sources: Qur'an 57:25 — 'And We sent down iron, wherein is great military might and benefits for the people.' (Saheeh International)
Science: iron is produced by stellar nucleosynthesis and dispersed by supernovae — Earth's iron has a stellar/cosmic origin.
